pairs.difference: A: the jacket and sash form a compact mass that fills the card's height well, with the arms reaching out on both sides and even air all round. B: the hat is a wide, low strip across the middle, with its brim almost at both side edges (margin 0.035). Its height of 0.475 is below every real card, leaving large empty bands above and below. It floats dead centre, whole and uncropped.
pairs.fix: Turn the hat three-quarters and tilt it so the crown rises higher. Draw it larger so it fills more of the card's height, and leave the brim slightly off centre.

pairs.difference: A: the pillow is one big blue shape filling the card, slightly tilted, and reads instantly. B: the photo card is small and narrow, with a 0.160 margin that is wider than any real card, so a lot of red background sits around it. At thumbnail size the rainbow stage lights inside the photo pull the eye before the card itself is named, and the signature competes as a second focus.
pairs.fix: Draw the photo card much larger so it fills most of the card. Simplify the picture inside it to one bold shape and make the signature smaller.

pairs.difference: The numbers are nearly identical. A: the band lies on a strong diagonal, tilted and three-quarter, like the real spyglass. B: the star faces straight on, upright and centred, with equal space on all sides. Only the small pin at right breaks the symmetry. That static, centred pose matches the generated lesson cards, but this is a weak signal.
pairs.fix: Turn the star three-quarters and tilt it about 15 degrees, with one point reaching towards the upper corner.

pairs.difference: A: the dock is cropped by the right edge and runs off the card like the cropped real cards, though the post and the ring share attention. B: the whole saloon is packed inside the frame, with an area of 0.632 far above the real maximum of 0.442. Wall fills the card edge to edge, with little sky left. At thumbnail size the many windows, doors and railings become an even, busy block with no single first read.
pairs.fix: Move in closer and let the right side of the building run off the card. Keep the swinging doors as the one large feature and show fewer windows.

pairs.difference: A: a wooden rail crosses the whole card edge to edge and cuts it in two, forming a second strong shape behind the saddle. The stirrup hangs low, and the margin is 0.100, just over the real limit. B: the ball is one huge, simple shape that is named instantly, though its area of 0.493 runs slightly over the real maximum.
pairs.fix: Draw only the saddle at a three-quarter angle, larger and tilted, on the plain background. Remove the full-width rail or crop it to a short piece.

pairs.difference: A: the tray sits at a three-quarter angle and fills the width, on a table that runs off the edges, and the raised cube gives a clear peak. B: the pot is upright and side-on, centred with a 0.119 margin that is wider than any real card. The fire below is the brightest spot and pulls the eye from the pot at thumbnail size, while the logs spread into a second cluster.
pairs.fix: Turn the pot three-quarters and draw it larger, closer to the card edges. Make the fire smaller and dimmer so the pot stays the first read.

pairs.difference: A: the rope is a thin line and a hollow loop, so its area of 0.153 is far below the real minimum of 0.264. The centre of the card is empty green, and the wooden post and beam cropped at bottom left carry more visual weight than the hero at thumbnail size. B: the pair of shoes is a solid colourful mass, though it sits low and has a short box height of 0.487 with empty orange above.
pairs.fix: Make the rope much thicker and larger. Fill the card with the coil and a tighter loop, and shrink or remove the wooden beam.

pairs.difference: A: the cactus is a narrow upright column placed dead centre, with a width of 0.537 and an area of 0.249, both below the real range. Wide empty pink sits on both sides and the pose is static. B: the machine is a solid three-quarter block with an area of 0.422, inside the real range, and it fills the card well. Its width of 0.581 is at the low end of real cards.
pairs.fix: Draw the cactus larger with its arms spread wider, and angle the pot slightly so it fills more of the card width.

pairs.difference: A: the boot is whole, floats on a slight diagonal and reads instantly, with the spur as a small accent. B: the cap is whole, tilted and wide, and also reads instantly. Both sit within or just at the real ranges on area, box size and margins, and neither has a competing element. Composition gives no reason to choose.

A: the bottle lies on a strong diagonal, with room around it. The bubbles and seaweed are busy but stay secondary, and its area of 0.237 is at the low end of real cards. B: three overlapping map sheets repeat the same shape, reach an area of 0.510 above the real maximum, and sit close to the edges with a 0.033 margin. The stack has no single clean silhouette, although the red X gives a clear focal point.
pairs.fix: Draw one single map, not a stack, tilted with a clear margin all round, and keep the red X as the main mark.

pairs.difference: A: the bus is a large three-quarter hero with buildings and clouds behind it. B: the locomotive is a large three-quarter hero with its nose close to the right edge. Both have the same area of 0.465, slightly above real cards, and similar tight margins of 0.030 and 0.026. Both read at once, so the framing does not separate them.

A: the wagon is whole, at three-quarter view, on a flat ground band, and its pole reaches left. B: the fountain is whole and centred, with its basin nearly reaching both sides (margin 0.035). Both are in range on area, height and margin, both read quickly, and neither has a rival focus.

pattern: Generated cards keep the whole object inside the frame, at centre or straight on, and rarely let it run off an edge the way the real lighthouse and desk computer are cropped. The clearest giveaways are hero size outside the real range, either packed too full (saloon, area 0.632) or too thin or narrow (rope 0.153, cactus width 0.537). A second giveaway is a supporting element that competes with the hero at thumbnail size, such as the campfire, the beam or the rail, which matches the props the lesson generators added around the lighthouse. Calls here are mostly low confidence, because the two cards in each pair show different objects, so size and framing depend partly on the object. Disclosure: in ten of the twelve pairs one card has a western theme, and p02 and p10 have none. I did not count that as evidence. It is not a composition finding, so p09, p11 and p12 stay neither, and p02 and p10 rest only on framing.
